## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṁghikacetapana-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 6) is a rule of training requiring forfeiture and confession within the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that if a nun exchanges away a requisite belonging to the Order that has been designated for a specific purpose, she commits an offense, requiring the item to be relinquished and the offense confessed. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Within the Pali tradition, full parallels are preserved in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-np6*) and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Nissaggiya Pācittiya 6), with related treatment in Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 8. Across other Buddhist monastic lineages, resembling rules are found in the Mahāsāṁghika-Lokottaravādin (*san-lo-bi-vb-np11*), Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Np 20*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Np25*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Np26*), and Mūlasarvāstivāda (*Lzh Mu Bi Vb Np 30*; *xct-mu-bi-vb-np30*) Vinayas.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
